label: last copy step of length-3 sequences (output of 3rd token, t=5)
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, and almost all of it on the final output step of length-3 sequences (t=5, outputting original token 2, two steps after <DEL>). That cell holds 87% of activation mass and 92% of the steps where the predicate holds are active. Weaker, lower-quartile activity occurs at the preceding step (t=4, recall_idx 1) in L=3 sequences, and at t=6 (recall_idx 2) in L=4 sequences. It is essentially silent in the original phase, on the delimiter step, and for L>=5. Magnitude is largest when the input at t=5 is f (or b); among the top examples the current input is nearly always f. The output token has little effect. Missed activations are mostly the weaker t=4 / L=4 cases.

issues: Main claims reproduce on test: P 0.919, R 0.710, F1 0.801, mass recall 0.869. On dev, t=5 holds 87.2% of activation mass and about 92% of L=3 t=5 steps are active.

The misses fall into the two weaker classes the explanation already names. L=3 recall_idx==1 (t=4) is 15% active and holds 6.2% of mass. L=4 recall_idx==2 is 3% active and holds 6.0% of mass. Together they cover most of the 978 missed test steps (13.1% of mass). Adding them to the predicate raises recall to 0.97 but drops precision to 0.16, so the narrow predicate is the right choice.

Minor overclaim: 'silent for L>=5' is not strictly true. Dev has about 92 activations at L>=5, scattered (for example 47 at t=11), holding about 0.7% of mass. Effectively silent, but not literally zero.

The input-token claim holds but is minor. Within the predicate, in_tok==f is active 100% of the time, but f makes up only about 6% of mass. Most of the activation comes from any input at L=3 t=5. Restricting the L=4 class to f/b inputs does not improve F1 (0.780).
The 210 test false positives (L=3 t=5 inactive) show no clear systematic token class in the samples (k, a, v, l, p, y inputs).

Data-source caveat: the user asked to run the baseline on features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, but scoring used features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store (dev split of 99,999 sequences). I could not confirm whether that store was built from the 1/5 subsample.
